+(``loss_mask`` marks the generated spans), and the stored conversation is in
+* A teacher that shares the student's token-id space is *not* cross-vocab
+  (see :func:`is_cross_vocab`); those runs keep the legacy path that sends the
+  student's own token ids to the teacher, byte for byte.
+* Otherwise each assistant turn is scored on its own: the conversation up to
+  and including that turn is rendered with the teacher's chat template (and the
+  run's teacher chat-template kwargs), tokenised with the teacher tokenizer,
+  and sent to the teacher as ``input_ids``.  This is the conversation as the
+  teacher would present it at that turn -- e.g. a template that only keeps the
+  latest turn's reasoning still judges every turn's reasoning while that turn
+  is the latest one, and tool calls are shown in the teacher's own tool-call
+* The teacher's per-token log-probs for the turn are mapped back onto the
+  student's generated tokens by character spans: identical substrings of the
+  student's raw turn text and the teacher-rendered turn text are aligned, and
+  inside them both tokenisations are cut at their shared boundaries.  The
+  first student token of each shared block receives the sum of the teacher
+  log-probs over the block (the teacher's log-prob of that exact text); any
+  other student token in the block starts inside a teacher token, where the
+  teacher has no distribution, so it gets no signal.  Student text that does
+  not appear in the teacher rendering at all (student-only scaffolding such
+  as its XML tool-call markup, reasoning a teacher template drops, ...) also
+  gets no signal.  "No signal" means ``teacher_log_probs`` equals the student
+  rollout log-prob, so the sampled-token reverse-KL term is zero there.
